subject: Observability POC — success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@fintechx.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: Observability POC

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. The team found Redwood's latency and KV cache examples useful. We'd like to move forward with a short POC focused on observability so our SREs can validate production behavior. Before we kick off, can you confirm the proposed success criteria and what Redwood will deliver during the trial?

High-level asks from our side:
- Dashboards for per-route latency, p50/p95/p99, token-level cost breakdowns
- Tracing across request -> model variant routing (to understand fallbacks)
- Log export (structured JSON) to our Splunk instance with request_id and model_version
- Metrics around cache hit rate and batching throughput

Desired timeline: 3 weeks from start, with a mid-point checkpoint.

Can you send a short evaluation plan, owners, and any sample dashboard mocks we can review?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Director of Platform Reliability, FintechX
attachments: product-demo-deck.pdf (slide stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fintechx.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@fintechx.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-11T18:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: Observability POC

Samir —

Appreciate the clear list. We've sketched a compact POC plan that lines up with your asks. Attached is a one-page success criteria doc and a dashboard mock. Summary below:

POC scope (3 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff, environment access, Splunk ingest test (owner: Marissa)
- Week 1: Instrumentation and baseline dashboards (owner: Jordan)
- Week 2: Tracing, routing visibility, cache tuning (owner: Marcus)
- Mid-week 2: Checkpoint demo + adjustments
- Week 3: Validation against success criteria + handoff notes

Success criteria (pass/fail checks):
- Observability: End-to-end trace that attributes 95% of requests to a model_version and route (target: 95% trace coverage)
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 450ms for your median request size during test load
- Cost telemetry: Token-level breakdown available in dashboards and matches Redwood billing within 5%
- Reliability: Automatic fallback events are surfaced in trace spans and dashboard alerts are triggered for >5% fallback rate
- Log export: Successful ingestion of structured JSON logs into your Splunk test index (sample schema attached)

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Dashboard JSON and mock PNG (attached)
- Trace spans with model_version and routing metadata
- Splunk ingestion sample pipeline (small config)
- Runbook for owners and recommended alert thresholds

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm POC start date (we can start as early as Mon 2027-03-15)
2) Provide Splunk test write endpoint + sample log index
3) 30-min kickoff with SRE + infra (Jordan + Marcus + your SREs)

I've attached poc_success_criteria.docx and a dashboard mock (observability_dashboard_mock.png). Let me know if you'd like any changes to success criteria.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0132
attachments: poc_success_criteria.docx, observability_dashboard_mock.png

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-12T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: Observability POC

Hi all —

Quick technical notes from the infra side so the SREs know what to expect:
- Dashboards: we'll provide a Grafana dashboard JSON with panels for p50/p95/p99, token-cost per route, cache hit rate, and fallback rate. Recommend the following panels:
  * Per-route latency heatmap
  * Token usage and cost per minute
  * Cache hit rate over sliding window (1/5/15m)
  * Fallback events counter + recent trace links
- Tracing: Redwood traces will include request_id, model_version, route, and fallback_reason. We can emit OTLP to your collector or push APM links.
- Logs: structured JSON with top-level keys: request_id, timestamp, model_version, route, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd. We'll give a sample ingestion config for Splunk HEC.
- Ownership: Jordan (instrumentation & dashboards), Marcus (routing/tracing, KV cache tuning). I'll own the mid-POC checkpoint demo.

A couple of clarifying Qs for FintechX:
1) Do you prefer Splunk HEC or S3-based log export for initial ingest?
2) Any rate limits we should be aware of for trace spans?

If Splunk HEC is ok, please share a test token + endpoint. Otherwise we can stage logs to S3 and you can pull them in.

Thanks,
Jordan
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
